milestone.title: mp-coordinator skill — planning + reviewing, master-planner + spec-grill + mp-code-review sub-mode integration

intent.outcome: After this ships, the `mp-coordinator` skill is the role-specific deep-dive for the coordinator agent (the planning + reviewing role per the two-agent / four-role architecture and the 12-stage mp-flow timeline). The skill covers the coordinator's domain in mp-flow: stages 1-4 (Draft → Groom → Specify → Approve — the spec-authoring domain where AC + scope are defined) and stages 8 + 10 (External review + Re-review — the round-2 review domain that consumes the runner's self-review). Three sub-modes: planning (with `master-planner` for stages 1-4), adversarial spec co-design (with `spec-grill` for weak specs), and reviewing (with the lesson-pattern pre-screeners and the round-2 review discipline). M121 absorbs the M99 mp-code-review content (the lesson-pattern library reference) as a sub-mode integration, plus the two-round review discipline and the L5 session-boundary enforcement.

problem.description: The two-agent / four-role architecture (coordinator = planning + reviewing, runner = executing + fixing) has a coordinator role but no canonical skill for it. The existing `master-planner` skill covers the planning sub-mode only; the existing `spec-grill` skill covers the adversarial sub-mode; and the M99 `mp-code-review` content (lesson patterns) covers the reviewing sub-mode. None of these is named 'coordinator' and none integrates the three sub-modes. The hand-off to the runner is implicit. Additionally, the L5 lesson ('same-session self-review is unreliable') is load-bearing for closing the M94 three-pass review, but no skill enforces the session-boundary discipline. M121 establishes the coordinator role skill and integrates the three sub-modes under it.

in_scope: `templates/skills/mp-coordinator/SKILL.md` (the role identity) — when an agent session is in coordinator role, the harness loads `mp-flow` + `mp-coordinator`; this SKILL.md is the role's identity, the sub-mode map, the stage ownership table (coordinator owns stages 1-4, 8, 10, 11, 12), the hand-off contract to the runner (with cross-link to M123), and the L5 session-boundary discipline.

`templates/skills/mp-coordinator/planning.md` (planning sub-mode) — the deep-dive of mp-flow stages 1-4 (Draft → Groom → Specify → Approve). References `master-planner` as the primary planning tool and back-links; doesn't duplicate its content (single-source invariant). Stages 1-4 are the spec-authoring domain: AC + scope + design_decisions are defined here, gating G1-G4 (spec_status) keep the milestone in `draft → groomed → ready` lifecycle states, and the Approve gate (stage 4) is the planner-to-runner hand-off entry documented in M123 (a).

`templates/skills/mp-coordinator/reviewing.md` (reviewing sub-mode) — the deep-dive of mp-flow stages 8 + 10 (External review + Re-review). The pre-screen runs lesson patterns from `docs/code-review-lessons.md` (M99 mp-code-review ships the procedural wrapper), the finding filing uses `mp reviews finding add --phase external`, the re-check after remediation uses `mp milestone verify`. Round 2 = coordinator's external review. Sessions are fresh per round per L5. Stages 8 → 9 → 10 iterate: a clean stage 10 advances to stage 11; new findings loop back to stage 9 (runner's Remediate, documented in M122).

`templates/skills/mp-coordinator/spec-co-design.md` (adversarial sub-mode) — references `spec-grill` as the primary tool; the coordinator invokes spec-grill for weak specs (most useful at stages 1-3, before Approve gates the work). Doesn't duplicate spec-grill content (single-source invariant).

Sub-skill integration test: an integration test that loads `mp-flow` + `mp-coordinator` + `master-planner` + `spec-grill` + `mp-code-review` (lessons) and walks a real planning → reviewing cycle against a fixture milestone, asserting the cross-mode hand-off contract (M123 four hand-off points) is functional, not just documented.

`mp install --skills=mp-coordinator` deploys the role identity + sub-mode references. The four sub-mode SKILLs (`master-planner`, `spec-grill`, `mp-code-review` as a sub-skill, `mp-flow` as a peer) are deployed via the existing install paths; the registry hooks them as a bundle.
out_of_scope: `master-planner` content — already shipped; M121 references it as the planning primary tool.
`spec-grill` content — already shipped; M121 references it as the adversarial primary tool.

Lesson-pattern library in `docs/code-review-lessons.md` — owned by `mp-code-review` (M99); M121's reviewing sub-mode consumes it as a back-link. Note: M99 was groomed but never executed; the Pattern: blocks for L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 are not yet authored. The lessons doc ships narrative only; the runnable pre-screen is deferred. M121 cross-links the lessons doc regardless.
The hand-off protocol deep-dive (what data passes, what session-boundary, what evidence at the four hand-off points) — M123.
Cross-role orchestration timeline — M120 (mp-flow). M121 references mp-flow's 12-stage timeline; M121 doesn't redefine the stages.

Replacing `mp-code-review` as a top-level skill. M99 is archived post-M121 (the lessons doc is the source of truth; `mp-code-review` SKILL.md stays registered as a peer for backward compatibility; M121's reviewing sub-mode is the role-specific wrapper). The pattern blocks for L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 remain deferred — see out_of_scope[3].

design_decisions.area: Three sub-modes (planning, spec-co-design, reviewing) as separate files vs. one big SKILL.md:
design_decisions.choice: Three sub-mode files (planning.md, reviewing.md, spec-co-design.md) under `templates/skills/mp-coordinator/`. SKILL.md is the role identity and stage ownership table: the coordinator owns mp-flow stages 1-4 (planning sub-mode), stages 8 + 10 (reviewing sub-mode), stages 11-12 (Document + Hand off, no sub-mode file needed). The sub-mode files are procedural deep-dives that reference the primary sub-skill (`master-planner`, `spec-grill`, `mp-code-review` respectively). The harness loads the role identity; the agent opens the sub-mode file when entering that stage range.
design_decisions.rationale: Three files match the three sub-modes naturally; one big SKILL.md would conflate sub-mode contents and re-document the primary sub-skills (single-source invariant violation). The role identity stays short and navigable; the sub-mode deep-dives stay focused.

design_decisions.area: Why three sub-skill references (master-planner, spec-grill, mp-code-review) instead of inlining their content:
design_decisions.choice: The three sub-skills already ship (master-planner since M27, spec-grill since M39, mp-code-review since M99). mp-coordinator references them as the primary tools. No content is inlined; mp-coordinator is the role-level orchestrator of the three.
design_decisions.rationale: Single source of truth. If mp-coordinator inlined the lesson patterns, the patterns would drift from `docs/code-review-lessons.md` (the canonical source). The integration test (AC-05) verifies the cross-mode flow is functional, not just documented.

design_decisions.area: M99 archival + mp-code-review peer model (12-stage alignment):
design_decisions.choice: M99 is archived once M121 lands. mp-coordinator's reviewing sub-mode covers mp-flow stages 8 + 10 (External review + Re-review); mp-code-review SKILL.md stays registered as a peer (not the canonical home) for the procedural wrapper over the lesson patterns. The patterns themselves ship in `docs/code-review-lessons.md` (the source of truth). Note: M99 was groomed but never executed; the runnable Pattern: blocks for L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 are not yet authored. The narrative lessons ship; the runnable pre-screen is a deferred work item. Post-archive: mp-code-review (skill) + M121 (reviewing sub-mode) are peers, both back-linking to the lessons doc; the runnable patterns are a future enhancement.
design_decisions.rationale: M99 ships a SKILL.md (the procedural wrapper); M121 ships a sub-mode file (the role-level reference). They're different artifacts that reference each other. M99 is archived (or kept as a historical anchor) per the user's call.

design_decisions.area: AC verification integrity check in reviewing sub-mode
design_decisions.choice: M121 reviewing sub-mode ships an AC verification integrity pre-flight: walks each AC verification field; resolves cargo test targets, Makefile targets, and bash/python scripts; flags unresolvable symbols as phase:external findings. Implemented as 'mp plan verify-ac <id>' and surfaced through 'mp milestone approve --dry-run' so the Approve gate at stage 4 fails when any AC has an unresolvable verification. The check runs in the coordinator reviewing session BEFORE the Approve hand-off (M123 AC-01 a).
design_decisions.rationale: M120 F-01 and F-02 (2026-07-08 review) were both AC-text defects: the verification fields referenced commands and test names that did not exist. The 2.x lean spec model (M82) treats verification as a free string with no compile-time link to the actual command. The only safety net today is post-hoc external review. Catching bogus verifications at review time is cheaper than at execute time (M122) or post-hoc. M123 hand-off point (a) consumes the integrity report; the runner rejects the hand-off if any AC has an unresolvable verification (defense in depth).

findings.description: make_targets_hardcoded_list: known_make_targets() is a static HashSet. New Makefile targets need code changes to be detected. Spec references make -pn integration.
cargo_test_fallback_too_optimistic: when no --test, --bin, or --lib flag present, falls through to generic crate found resolution. Trailing test names after -- are silently ignored.
test_path_regex_truncates_quoted_paths: extract_test_path regex uses non-whitespace match which breaks on paths with spaces in quotes
resolve_script_and_python_dedup: resolve_script_path and resolve_python_script have nearly identical logic, can be merged into one function
dead_code_slashdot_prefix: extract_command_path has ./ check both at top and in prefix slice, the prefix slice entry is unreachable

deploy_test_wrong_file: mp_coordinator_deploys_with_sub_modes test lives in coordinator_role_skill.rs but AC-06 spec says --test install_skills_v2. Either move the test or update the AC verification string.

verify-ac resolver (crates/mp/src/commands/plan_verify_ac.rs:117-119) recognizes only `cargo test` and `cargo nextest` as resolvable command forms. Other runnable cargo subcommands — `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo build`, `cargo check`, `cargo bench`, `cargo doc` — fall through to the `unknown` branch with detail "unrecognized command form; cannot statically resolve: <verification>". This is a coverage gap because many ACs across the project use these commands: M127 5/5 ACs (`cargo clippy -p mp --all-targets exits 0` etc.), M128 AC-01 (`cargo fmt -- --check exits 0`), M129 3/3 ACs (`cargo clippy` verifications), M130 2/2 ACs (`make test` + clippy), plus 30+ other milestones. Remediation: extend `resolve_ac_verification` to recognize the canonical cargo subcommands and report them as `status: recognized` (or `status: runtime-only` — a new enum value indicating the command form is valid and runnable but cannot be statically resolved against the codebase). Add unit tests for each recognized subcommand. Optionally: add a `manual:`-prefixed branch for "runtime-only" commands that the reviewer confirms via `manual:` override.
findings.author: external:review-m121

findings.description: The Approve gate (crates/mp/src/commands/milestone.rs:431) only fails on `status: UNRESOLVABLE`. The `status: unknown` branch — which is what `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo build`, etc. currently resolve to (see F-01) — is silently ignored. The integrity report (verify-ac report, attached as `gates: [{code: "verify-ac", report: ...}]`) does contain the unknown entries, but the gate errors list is empty. Effect: a coordinator reviewing the integrity report sees unknown entries that look like warnings, but the approve succeeds anyway. This contradicts M121 AC-09 (catch bogus verifications at review time) because the most common case (cargo clippy, cargo fmt, cargo build) is the case the gate lets through. Remediation: change the gate check to also fail (or warn, with --strict option) when any AC has status: unknown. The integrity report surface is enough — the coordinator reads it and resolves the unknowns (typically: switch to cargo test equivalent, prefix with manual:, or accept the unknown via --strict flag).
findings.author: external:review-m121

findings.description: No end-to-end test asserts that `mp milestone approve --dry-run` on a milestone with a bogus AC verification (e.g., `cargo test -p nonexistent_crate --test nonexistent`) exits non-zero with the M121 validation issue surfaced in the gate errors. The wiring is in crates/mp/src/commands/milestone.rs:428-447 (the verify_ac::verify_ac result is matched against UNRESOLVABLE and pushed as a ValidationIssue), but plan_verify_ac.rs only tests the `mp plan verify-ac <id>` CLI surface — it does not drive a milestone through to ready and run approve --dry-run. Without this test, future refactors of the approve gate could silently break the verify-ac integration. Remediation: add a test in crates/mp/tests/write_dry_run.rs (or a new crates/mp/tests/approve_dry_run_verify_ac.rs) that creates a milestone with a bogus AC verification, drives it to set-spec-status ready, and asserts approve --dry-run exits non-zero with the M121 validation issue text present in stderr or the structured gate errors JSON.
